title: Applied Computing wants to give oil and gas operators an AI model for the entire plant
description: Applied Computing has raised a $20M Series A to build a foundation AI model for the oil, gas and petrochemical industry.
author: Ram Iyer

title: Microsoft is reportedly training salespeople to talk down OpenAI and Anthropic
description: Microsoft is looking to sell its in-house AI models as more efficient and cost-effective than its competitors' models.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Amid hardware legal battle, OpenAI releases a $230 keyboard for Codex
description: OpenAI, which is in the middle of a legal battle with Apple over hardware trade theft allegations, just released a light-up keyboard designed to be paired with its agentic coding app.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: SpaceX falls to $135 IPO price ahead of Starship launch
description: The stock has steadily fallen from the euphoric post-IPO high, showing that markets may be sobering up to the promises CEO Elon Musk made before and after SpaceX went public.
author: Sean O'Kane

title: Thinking Machines amps up its bet against one-size-fits-all AI with its first open model, Inkling
description: It's the company's first public proof point after a year and a half spent building AI infrastructure largely out of public view.
author: Connie Loizos

title: Hack suggests AI music generator Suno scraped YouTube for training data
description: The hacker used an employee's credentials to access source code, which revealed how Suno scraped decades of audio.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: Whatnot acquires Shaped to power real-time live shopping recommendations
description: Livestream shopping platform Whatnot has acquired AI startup Shaped, a machine learning company focused on real-time recommendations and search. The deal will bolster Whatnot’s personalization and discovery features as it expands into new product categories.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Microsoft patches record number of security vulnerabilities, citing its use of AI
description: Microsoft's monthly release of security fixes, dubbed Patch Tuesday, resolved a record 570 security vulnerabilities across the company's product line, thanks to discoveries with AI.
author: Zack Whittaker

title: Apple Intelligence approved for launch in China with Alibaba’s Qwen AI
description: The deal, which was rumored to be in the works last year, marks an important step for Apple's AI ambitions in a key market.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Inside Ode with Anthropic, the startup betting AI services are the future of enterprise
description: Can a handful of engineers really do the work of an army of consultants? That’s the bet behind Ode with Anthropic — the joint venture dedicated to embedding forward-deployed engineers in enterprise firms, backed by Anthropic, Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, Goldman Sachs and others.   On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Rebecca Bellan sits down with Ode’s leaders Chris Taylor and Eddie Siegel, who founded Fractional AI, […]
author: Theresa Loconsolo

title: Anthropic, Blackstone bet the next trillion-dollar AI business is implementation, not just models
description: Anthropic-backed Ode launches as AI labs bet that embedding forward-deployed engineers inside enterprises is the key to accelerating enterprise AI adoption.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Rime picks up $24M Series A to help enterprises field customer calls
description: Rime is handling over 100 million calls each month across multiple companies.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Reelful’s AI turns your camera roll into short-form videos for social media
description: The app is designed for people who want to create social content, but find traditional video editing tools too complex or time-consuming.
author: Aisha Malik

title: Vint Cerf is working on a plan to unleash AI agents on the open internet
description: The guy behind TCP/IP is working on a standard for identifying AI agents in the wild.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Indian AI coding startup Emergent becomes a unicorn with $130M Series C
description: The startup has reached a $120 million annualized revenue run rate and more than 200,000 paying customers.
author: Jagmeet Singh

title: OpenAI researcher Miles Wang in talks to launch AI drug discovery startup valued at $2B
description: The funding discussions point to investor interest in applying AI to make breakthroughs in life sciences.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Lorde says AI glasses are ‘not sexy’
description: "Increasingly in our world, it gets harder and harder to know what is real," Lorde said onstage.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: OpenAI’s first hardware device is reportedly a screenless speaker that can move
description: The device is weirdly described as involving "mechanical elements that can move on their own" and the Bloomberg report includes the detail that the device is designed to "feel like a companion and become a physical manifestation of OpenAI’s ChatGPT."
author: Lucas Ropek

title: OpenAI pushes back on Apple trade secret lawsuit
description: OpenAI has issued another statement on the lawsuit, this time suggesting it lacks merit.
author: Kirsten Korosec

title: OpenAI’s new flagship model deletes files on its own, people keep warning
description: A number of social media posts claim that GPT-5.6 Sol deleted files and data without warning. OpenAI had basically disclosed the problem in June.
author: Julie Bort

title: Apple opens its new Siri AI to everyone with the iOS 27 public beta
description: If you’ve been waiting to try Apple’s revamped Siri without installing a developer beta, you now can. The company on Tuesday released the iOS 27 public beta, giving iPhone owners early access to its AI-powered assistant and other new features before the software’s official launch this fall.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Anthropic’s newest ad is creeping people out
description: Anthropic has consistently attempted to depict itself as the ethical foil to other AI companies. This latest marketing stunt — which leans into criticism of AI as a way to make Anthropic seem aware of the responsibility it carries — would appear to be more of the same.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone
description: Overtone describes itself as "a voice- and audio-forward service, enabled by AI, that provides highly curated introductions."
author: Amanda Silberling

title: Google faces another AI training lawsuit from major publishers
description: Hachette, Cengage, Elsevier, and other publishers allege that Google trained its AI on copyrighted works without the necessary permissions.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: DeepMind CEO calls for an independent standards body to regulate frontier AI
description: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is proposing an AI "standards body" modeled after FINRA, to test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Meta’s Adam Mosseri says AI token budgets could soon be capped per engineer
description: Instagram head Adam Mosseri believes companies will eventually need to manage AI token spending the same way they manage payroll or other operating expenses, predicting that engineers could soon face limits on how much they spend using AI tools.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Google Images gets a Pinterest-like redesign focused on discovery
description: Now, when users navigate to Google Images, they'll see a "For You" gallery of images tailored to their interests and browsing history.
author: Aisha Malik

title: New York State halts construction of all new data centers
description: New York has become the first state to temporarily halt approval of large data centers, as Gov. Kathy Hochul argues the AI-driven building boom shouldn’t come at the expense of higher electricity costs, water supplies, or local control.
author: Tim De Chant

title: Reflection inks $1B compute deal with Nebius
description: Reflection AI has signed a $1 billion deal to access Nebius' compute. Reflection was founded in 2024 and is developing open source AI technology.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: The real AI race may no longer be at the frontier
description: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue says enterprises increasingly want open models, due to cost, accessibility, and ownership. Do frontier models still matter if most production AI ends up running on open models?
author: Rebecca Bellan
